subject: Adopter toolkit: SDK integration blueprint, timeouts & retry policy

Subject: Adopter toolkit kickoff — SDK surface area questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the intro call yesterday — Pellion is excited to get started. Before we lock a technical kickoff, Daniel and I wanted to run a quick list of integration items so we can scope our internal sprint. High level asks:

- Which SDKs do you recommend for a Node 18 backend (server-side) vs a React Native thin client?
- Do you have recommended default timeouts and retry strategies for short-lived interactive requests (chat) versus batched inference (embeddings)?
- Any gotchas for endpoint migration (we plan to move from a staged Sandbox endpoint to Redwood Hosted within our pilot window — want to avoid token invalidation and double-counting requests).

If you can sketch a short ‘adopter toolkit’ or checklist with code snippets, that would help our PM and infra lead triage effort.

Attaching our initial mutual action plan so we align on dates.

Alex

Alex — great questions, and glad to hear the PM timeline looks healthy. I pulled together a short adopter toolkit with the immediate guidance and a few runnable snippets. Monica will add the endpoint migration checklist and Vanessa will coordinate the implementation handoff / support cadence.

Quick answers up front:
- Node 18: use Redwood's official node-sdk (stable) with the streaming client for chat, and the batch client for embeddings. React Native: use the REST client or the community RN shim to avoid heavy native deps.
- Timeouts & retries: interactive (chat) -> socket/stream timeout 20s, per-request token timeout 30s; retry on 5xx or network errors with exponential backoff starting at 200ms, max 5 retries. Batch -> request timeout 2m, fewer retries (3) but enable idempotency keys.
- Endpoint migration: rotate keys and drain the sandbox worker pool before cutover; use request deduplication headers to avoid double submission.

I've attached a zip of SDK snippets and a CSV matrix for recommended timeout/retry parameters. Proposed next step: 30-min tech kickoff Monday to review the Mutual Action Plan and assign owners.

Attachments: pellion_sdk_snippets.zip (zip), sdk_timeout_matrix.csv (csv)

Hi Alex / Daniel — following up with concrete implementation notes and a minimal sample for Node that demonstrates resilient request patterns. Paste below is intentionally small; full samples are in the attached ZIP.

--- sample Node snippet (pseudo) ---
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/sdk');
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY, timeoutMs: 30000 });

async function callChat(payload) {
  let attempt = 0;
  const maxRetries = 5;
  while (attempt <= maxRetries) {
    try {
      const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', messages: payload });
      return res;
    } catch (err) {
      if (isTransient(err) && attempt < maxRetries) {
        await sleep(200 * Math.pow(2, attempt)); // exponential backoff
        attempt++;
        continue;
      }
      throw err;
    }
  }
}

Key operational recommendations:
- Use idempotency-key header for all batched scoring and webhook-driven retries (X-Idempotency-Key).
- Instrument request_id and model_version in logs to make rollout regressions debuggable.
- For streaming chat: prefer socket keepalive and a 20s chunk timeout; do not aggressively retry mid-stream — instead, failover to a fresh request and reconcile client-side state.
- Endpoint migration steps (short):
  1) Create new API key scoped to the hosted environment.
  2) Start sending mirrored traffic (5–10%) with a custom header X-RW-Mirror to exercise hosted path.
  3) Drain sandbox queue and mark last-processed cursor.
  4) Cutover traffic, rotate keys, and run a quick token-count audit.

I'll join Monday's kickoff and bring a short ops checklist.

Alex / team — short answers to your infra questions and an owner map for Monday: 

- Mirrored traffic billing: mirrored traffic marked with X-RW-Mirror will not be billed (we track it as a test stream). I'll ask billing to whitelist the HubSpot pilot ID during your pilot window — Monica will follow up with the exact HubSpot deal ID in the kickoff.
- Idempotency: SDK will not silently reuse keys across independent requests. We recommend generating and passing X-Idempotency-Key from your side for batched operations; the SDK exposes a helper (Idempotency.generate()) in the snippets.

Owners & immediate next steps: 
- Stephanie (CS): schedule and lead Monday kickoff, confirm pilot dates in the Mutual Action Plan.
- Monica (Impl): run the mirrored traffic test and validate telemetry within 48 hours after kickoff.
- Vanessa (Support): provision 24/7 escalation channel during the 2-day cutover window and share PagerDuty stub.
